elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: New sentence: "the Servicer grants the Issuer and the Depositor, and on written notice their respective Affiliates, a license to use its processes, procedures, models, servicing software and other applications..." — Affiliates are within the grant (albeit conditioned on written notice, which satisfies the fallback formulation).

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The grant runs only to "the Issuer and the Depositor, and on written notice their respective Affiliates". The phrase "or to have serviced, the Receivables" describes permitted purpose, not a grant of rights to contractors; no express extension to contractors or subservicers acting on Issuer/Depositor's behalf appears. Drafter concedes contractor coverage was not added.

The inserted grant is silent on consideration and duration; it is characterised neither as paid-up nor as subscription, and no perpetuity language ("perpetual", "for so long as") is present. Whether the paid-up condition is triggered cannot be determined from the operative text.

No "irrevocable" (or "non-revocable") wording in the inserted sentence, and the text does not identify the licence as paid-up, so the condition's applicability is indeterminate. Note the retained sentence contains no at-will revocation right, so nothing expressly permits Servicer revocation.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the grant is a servicing-purpose licence under a transfer and servicing agreement with no subscription, fee or term structure attached to it, so no subscription-licence termination standard is required.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Transferability is confined to "a successor of the Issuer or the Depositor by merger or acquisition" — narrower than transferability to successors generally (e.g. successors by operation of law, reorganisation or asset sale).

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: "the Servicer grants the Issuer and the Depositor, and on written notice their respective Affiliates, a license to use..."; "Affiliate" is a defined term (p0579), so no undefined capitalised term is introduced.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: "...which license is transferable to a successor of the Issuer or the Depositor by merger or acquisition."

reasons: Fallback level is complete: both fallback elements are met in operative language (Affiliates on written notice; transferability to an M&A successor of the Issuer or Depositor). The finding is therefore position-complete at the declared fallback target.

Preferred level is not complete. To reach it the drafter would need to (a) extend the grant expressly to "contractors and subservicers acting on the Issuer's or Depositor's behalf", (b) make the licence "perpetual and irrevocable" (or state it is fully paid-up and perpetual/irrevocable), and (c) broaden transferability from "a successor by merger or acquisition" to "Customer's successors and permitted assigns". These are noted, not required, since the fallback is satisfied.

Minimality holds: the change is a single added sentence for a clause that did not exist; the Servicer's existing carve-out (Successor Servicer, third parties, transfer/confidentiality restrictions and legal, regulatory, privacy and data protection protections) is retained verbatim with no deletions. "Customer" (Issuer/Depositor) is not defined to include Affiliates, so the affiliate extension is not duplicative.

The "Notwithstanding the preceding sentence" opener is narrowly targeted at the immediately preceding no-obligation-to-license sentence and is necessary to avoid a directly contradictory retained sentence; it is not a broad override of the transition provisions and so does not fail minimality.

Intent is preserved: the Section 7.4/7.5 transition allocation, delivery obligations and the Servicer's restricted-materials protections survive, subordinated only to the extent of the new grant by the express priority language; no dangling cross-reference or undefined term is created.

Residual drafting point (not a defect at the fallback): the grant's purpose scope "as necessary to service, or to have serviced, the Receivables" combined with the retained Successor Servicer carve-out could be read as leaving downstream use by a Successor Servicer contested; the notwithstanding clause resolves priority, but express contractor/subservicer wording would remove the ambiguity.
